data.description:
## Summary

The mutation sandbox's Linux write-deny (`bwrap`) has **no gating CI lane**. The
enforcement tests in `tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py` are gated on
`skipif(mutation_sandbox.probe() is None)`. GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners ship
bubblewrap but DENY unprivileged user namespaces (`setting up uid map: Permission
denied`), so the functional probe correctly returns `None` there and every enforcement
test SKIPS. The leg goes green having proven nothing about Linux enforcement.

This is the silent-skip failure mode: the signal that would report a broken Linux
sandbox is indistinguishable from the signal for a healthy one.

`bwrap` enforcement WAS verified by hand during the `e668-b496-e264-4283` work, in a
`ubuntu:24.04` container: a write outside the allow-list was denied, a write inside
succeeded, and `rm -rf <protected>/*` was denied with the target surviving. That is a
one-off manual measurement, not a regression control — nothing re-checks it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three-probe `bwrap` enforcement test executes (does NOT skip) on a gating CI
      lane. Verified by asserting the test's outcome is `passed`, not `skipped`, in that
      lane's report.
- [ ] The lane FAILS if the sandbox stops enforcing — proven by temporarily
      substituting a no-op wrapper and observing the lane go red, not asserted.
- [ ] A skipped enforcement test is treated as a FAILURE on the lane intended to prove
      Linux enforcement, so the silent-skip mode cannot return.
- [ ] The mechanism is portable: it does not depend on a feature unique to one CI
      provider (`project.portability`). A container image or an equivalent
      locally-runnable environment satisfies this; a GitHub-Actions-only construct does
      not.

## Definition of Done

- Linux `bwrap` write-denial is proven by an automated, gating control.
- The control is shown to go red when enforcement is removed.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Notes

Discovered from `e668-b496-e264-4283`: its plan-review BLOCKED on the contradiction
between an acceptance criterion claiming a green `ubuntu-latest` leg proves Linux
enforcement and another recording that the runners deny unprivileged user namespaces.
The same gap was raised as an advisory finding by the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on change
2256 (patch sets 1, 3 and 4).
data.title: Linux bwrap enforcement has no gating CI lane (tests skip silently)
